convertibility_reason: Uses custom signal filter CH_HM_MFI from external .mqh library (Expert\Signal\MySignals\ACH_HM_MFI.mqh). The trading logic depends on this custom signal module which is not a built-in MT5 indicator, requiring manual analysis of the custom signal class to replicate entry/exit rules in Python.

other_exits: Signal-based close when CH_HM_MFI signal strength drops below Signal_ThresholdClose (20)

custom_logic_notes: The EA uses the MQL5 Standard Library Expert Advisor framework (CExpert, CExpertSignal, CMoneyFixedLot, CTrailingNone). The actual entry/exit logic is encapsulated in the CH_HM_MFI custom signal filter class from ACH_HM_MFI.mqh. Signal threshold open=40 and close=20 suggest the filter produces a weighted vote (0-100 scale) where long signals are generated when the composite score exceeds 40 and short signals when it drops below -40 (or the inverse for close). The CExpertSignal framework aggregates filter votes with weights; with a single filter at weight=1.0, the filter's LongCondition/ShortCondition return values directly determine trading. Expert_EveryTick=false means the EA evaluates on new bar only, not every tick. SL and TP are both 0 indicating the EA relies entirely on signal reversal for exits with no hard stops.
python_conversion_notes: Must read ACH_HM_MFI.mqh to extract the actual MFI+MA crossover/comparison logic in LongCondition() and ShortCondition() methods. The CExpert framework handles position management automatically - Python version will need manual position tracking. MFI (Market Facilitation Index) is available in most Python charting libraries (e.g., ta-lib MFI function). The threshold-based voting system needs to be replaced with direct boolean conditions. No SL/TP means Python version should implement signal-reversal exit only. The MoneyFixedLot at 0.1 lots is trivial to replicate. No pending order management needed - all entries are market orders. Key risk: zero SL/TP means unlimited loss per trade; consider adding a default safety stop in Python version.
